scope: amendment 1 to provenance/model_selection_policy_v2.json, made after evaluation 2 stopped and before evaluation 3; it changes how the AdarEdit reference is sourced and checked, and nothing else

made_after.what_happened: the session stopped on Artery at its cross-check of our CPU AdarEdit scores against the AdarEdit column of PNAS's saved session (a same-device tolerance applied to a CPU-vs-GPU comparison); rows, pairs and labels matched and PNAS's published-baseline check passed
made_after.outcome_seen: none: no metric of any model was computed or written, the registry was unchanged

changes: The AdarEdit reference is the per-row AdarEdit scores and calls of PNAS's saved session (results/adarpro/final_locked_test/), so AdarEdit's numbers are exactly the published ones. They must follow the checkpoint threshold and reproduce the published baseline (PNAS's own check). Our CPU rescoring of the same checkpoints is kept as a check: per row within 1e-3, with differing calls allowed only where both scores lie within 1e-3 of the threshold.
Every check on every endpoint runs before any metric is computed or any file written (two passes).
PNAS's saved predictor must reproduce its published metrics within 1e-6 on score-based metrics (AUROC, AUPRC, Brier) and exactly on count-based ones.
Outputs of evaluation 3: results/adarpro/final_locked_test_v3/ and figures/final_v3/.
unchanged: headline, comparators, contrasts, metrics, intervals, replicates, seeds, thresholds, reading rule, failure rule, downstream analyses
